'429':
          description: |
            The file may not have been stored. Phones don't retry on 429, and nothing is lost:
            app.log carries its lines into the next upload, and the other files are full copies
            every time. One of:

            - KEY_EXISTS: another file of this type from this phone was stored in the same
              millisecond. Nothing is overwritten, and the next upload gets a new receive time
              (ADR 0011).
            - STORAGE_FAILED: S3 failed the write or it ran past its 60 s deadline. Once the whole
              body was sent, S3 can still commit the object after the deadline. Never 503.
    head:
      summary: Always 404
      description: Each upload stands alone, so there is never a stored file to compare against.
      operationId: headLog

content.text:
When the S3 write fails or passes its 60 s deadline, the upload service returns **429 Too Many Requests**, with rejection reason `STORAGE_FAILED`. It must **never return 503**.

- Phones don't retry on 429, and nothing is lost: `app.log` carries its lines into the next upload, and the other file types are full copies each time.
- After a timeout the file may still have been stored, because S3 can commit the object after the deadline once the whole body was sent.
- The 60 s deadline is shorter than the ALB's 120 s idle timeout. That way the phone gets the service's 429 instead of a timeout from the ALB (ADR 0005).
